results.title: Exhibition: A Life Composed: Chin Whai's Journey Through Music, Literature & Charity
results.description:
Born Tan Leng Gek (陈龙玉) (1938 – ), Chin Whai (秦淮) rose to prominence in the 1970s, when his songs captured the hearts of audiences across Singapore, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia. Known for his distinctive vocal style and deeply expressive ballads, he became affectionately known as the “King of Ballads”.

Yet, long before he took to the stage as a singer, Chin Whai began his career as a writer, with works appearing in publications such as Sin Chew Daily and Nanyang Siang Pau. He published his first book at the age of 22 and went on to produce 11 volumes of poetry, prose and essays. A prolific and versatile creative, he also explored the visual arts as a painter and illustrator.

After stepping away from the spotlight, Chin Whai devoted himself to giving back to society. Over the years, he headlined numerous charity events, using his music to raise funds and support those in need. His enduring commitment to philanthropy earned him another affectionate title—the “Charity King of Songs”.

Part of NUS Libraries Chinese Popular Culture Collection series, this exhibition celebrates the the multifaceted creative life and enduring legacy of Chin Whai through a selection of materials from his private papers, generously donated to NUS Libraries. Bringing together his writings, artwork, photographs and other personal materials, the exhibition offers a glimpse into the many facets of an artist whose creative journey has spanned music, literature and the visual arts.

results.title: Exhibition: Youth, Hope & Unity: Reflections on Pope Francis's Historic Visit to Singapore
results.description:
This exhibition documents His Holiness Pope Francis' visit to Singapore in September 2024 as part of his Asia-Pacific tour – including his address at the National University of Singapore's University Cultural Centre.

Featuring objects, photographs, video footage, and printed materials from the occasion, the display centres on the hand-crafted chairs used by Pope Francis and President Tharman Shanmugaratnam during the event.

The exhibition also presents replay footage of the Pope's address, selected publications from the Library's collection, and a section highlighting student-led interfaith initiatives at NUS.

results.title: NUS Libraries Collections Game Jam 2026
results.description:
Kick off the Game Jam with us!

Learn more about the challenge, explore the featured NUS Libraries collections, meet other participants, and find out what you will need to create and submit your game.

Come with an idea, a team, or simply your curiosity. We’ll help you get started!

Please note that you will need to register in two places:

  1. Sign up on this page so that we can verify your eligibility as an NUS student.
  2. Join the Game Jam on itch.io to access the full jam details and submit your game.

For more information and to join the jam on itch.io, visit:
https://itch.io/jam/nus-libraries-collections-2026
results.more_info:
NUS Libraries Collections Game Jam 2026

Terms and Conditions

By registering for and participating in the NUS Libraries Collections Game Jam 2026 (“Game Jam”), participants agree to the following terms and conditions.

1. Eligibility

1.1 The Game Jam is open only to currently enrolled undergraduate and postgraduate students of the National University of Singapore (“NUS”) who are pursuing an NUS degree programme. Participants enrolled solely in continuing education, professional education, executive education, certificate, or other non-degree programmes are not eligible.

1.2 Participants must remain enrolled as NUS students during the Game Jam period.

1.3 NUS staff members are not eligible to participate, including staff members who are concurrently enrolled as NUS students.

1.4 Participants may be required to provide their NUS email address or other reasonable proof of student status for verification.

1.5 The organisers reserve the right to reject or disqualify any registration where eligibility cannot be verified.

1.6 Individuals involved in organising, administering, facilitating workshops for, or judging the Game Jam are not eligible to compete.

2. Registration

2.1 Participants must register through the official NUS Libraries registration page and join the Game Jam on itch.io.

2.2 Registration on only one of the two platforms will not be considered complete.

2.3 Participants are responsible for ensuring that the information submitted during registration is accurate.

2.4 Registration and participation are free of charge.

3. Team Participation

3.1 Participants must take part in teams of two to three members.

3.2 Every member of a team must meet the eligibility requirements and complete the required registration.

3.3 A participant may belong to only one team and contribute to only one competition entry.

3.4 Changes to team membership after the registration deadline are subject to the organisers’ approval.

3.5 Prizes are awarded to the team as a whole. Each winning team will receive one prize box containing three prize items, regardless of whether the team has two or three members. Team members are responsible for deciding how the items will be distributed.

4. Game Development and Submission

4.1 Each participant or team may submit only one game.

4.2 Games must be created specifically for the Game Jam and must respond meaningfully to the stated challenge or featured NUS Libraries collections.

4.3 Entries must be submitted through the official itch.io Game Jam page by the stated submission deadline.

4.4 Late, incomplete, inaccessible, corrupted, or incorrectly submitted entries may not be accepted.

4.5 Participants are responsible for testing their games and ensuring that judges can access and play them using the submission instructions provided.

4.6 The organisers are not responsible for technical problems, internet disruptions, file corruption, itch.io account issues, or other circumstances that prevent an entry from being submitted successfully.

5. Originality and Permitted Resources

5.1 Entries must be the participants’ own work.

5.2 Participants may use pre-existing game engines, frameworks, code libraries, templates, fonts, audio, artwork, and other third-party resources, provided that they have the legal right or appropriate licence to use them.

5.3 All third-party resources must be appropriately credited in the game, its documentation, or its itch.io submission page.

5.4 Entries must not infringe any copyright, trademark, privacy, publicity, or other rights belonging to another person or organisation.

5.5 The organisers may request evidence of the source or licence of any material used in an entry.

6. Use of Generative AI

6.1 Generative AI tools may be used unless otherwise stated by the organisers.

6.2 Participants must disclose any substantial use of generative AI, including its use to produce artwork, audio, writing, code, or other game assets.

6.3 Participants remain responsible for the accuracy, originality, legality, and suitability of all AI-generated or AI-assisted content included in their entries.

6.4 Entries containing undisclosed or improperly used AI-generated material may be penalised or disqualified.

7. Use of NUS Libraries Collections

7.1 Participants must observe any copyright, access, attribution, or reuse conditions associated with the featured NUS Libraries materials.

7.2 Access to a collection item does not automatically mean that the item may be reproduced, modified, or distributed without restriction.

7.3 Participants must include any acknowledgements or attribution statements specified by NUS Libraries.

7.4 Collection materials must not be used in a misleading, defamatory, discriminatory, or disrespectful manner.

8. Intellectual Property

8.1 Participants retain ownership of the original intellectual property they create for their entries.

8.2 By submitting an entry and its project files, participants grant NUS and NUS Libraries a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to access, use, reproduce, modify, adapt, maintain and further develop the submitted game and project files for educational, research, archival, exhibition, promotional and other non-commercial purposes. This may include fixing technical issues, updating the game for compatibility, adding or revising content, adapting the game for future programmes, and making the game available to others.

This licence will continue after the conclusion of the Game Jam.

8.3 Where reasonably practicable, the original team will be acknowledged when the game or an adapted version of it is displayed or used.

8.4 This licence includes permission to use screenshots, gameplay recordings, trailers, project descriptions, team names and other submitted materials in NUS and NUS Libraries communications.

8.5 The organisers will not commercially sell or license a participant’s game to another party without obtaining additional permission from the relevant participant or team.

8.6 Participants must ensure that they have the necessary rights to share all submitted project files and to grant the licence described in this section. Third-party materials may only be included where their licences allow them to be shared, modified and reused for these purposes.

9. Indemnity

By participating in the Game Jam, each participant agrees to indemnify and hold harmless the organisers against any claims, losses, damages, liabilities, costs and expenses, including reasonable legal costs, arising from or relating to:

  1. the participant’s development, submission, distribution or use of the game;
  2. any allegation that the game or its contents infringe a third party’s intellectual property or other rights;
  3. any breach of these Terms and Conditions by the participant; or
  4. any unlawful, negligent or wrongful act or omission by the participant in connection with the Game Jam.

10. Content and Conduct

10.1 Entries must not contain unlawful, hateful, discriminatory, harassing, defamatory, sexually explicit, malicious, or otherwise inappropriate content.

10.2  Entries must not contain malware, spyware, harmful code, unauthorised data collection, or functionality intended to damage or interfere with another system.

10.3 Participants must behave respectfully towards other participants, judges, organisers, speakers, and members of the public.

10.4 Harassment, intimidation, plagiarism, cheating, sabotage, or disruptive conduct may result in removal from the Game Jam.

11. Judging

11.1 Eligible entries will be assessed according to the judging criteria published by the organisers.

11.2 The organisers may appoint judges and amend the judging arrangements where necessary.

11.3 Judges may decline to assess an entry that cannot be accessed, launched, understood, or played within the available judging period.

11.4 All decisions made by the judges and organisers are final. The organisers will not enter into any correspondence or appeals concerning the judging process or results.

11.5 The organisers reserve the right not to award a prize in a category if no entry meets the required standard.

12. Prizes

12.1 Prizes are non-transferable and cannot be exchanged for cash unless otherwise stated.

12.2 Participants must satisfy all eligibility and verification requirements before receiving a prize.

12.3 Prizes are awarded per team, not per individual participant.

12.4 Each winning team will receive one prize box containing three prize items. A team of two members will still receive the full prize box, including the additional item.

12.5 Participants are responsible for collecting their prizes by the stated deadline. Unclaimed prizes may be forfeited.

13. Publicity, Photography and Recordings

13.1 Photographs, video recordings, screenshots, or other documentation may be taken during Game Jam activities.

13.2 These materials may be used by NUS and NUS Libraries for event documentation, reporting, education, and publicity.

13.3 Participants who have concerns about appearing in photographs or recordings should inform the organisers before attending an in-person activity.

14. Personal Data

14.1 Personal data collected through registration will be used for purposes related to administering the Game Jam, including eligibility verification, participant communications, event management, judging, prize administration, and reporting.

14.2 Participants’ information may be shared with relevant NUS units, judges, event partners, or service providers only where reasonably necessary for these purposes.

14.3 Participants are also subject to itch.io’s applicable terms and privacy practices when creating an account or submitting an entry through that platform.

15. Disqualification

15.1 The organisers may reject or disqualify an entry or participant for:

  • providing false or misleading registration information;
  • failing to meet the eligibility requirements;
  • missing the submission deadline;
  • plagiarism or intellectual-property infringement;
  • failure to disclose third-party or AI-generated materials;
  • breaching the code of conduct;
  • tampering with the judging or submission process; or
  • breaching any of these terms and conditions.

15.2 Disqualification may take place before or after judging. Where appropriate, prizes may be withdrawn or reassigned.

16. Changes, Postponement or Cancellation

16.1 The organisers reserve the right to amend the schedule, format, judging arrangements, prizes, rules, or other aspects of the Game Jam where reasonably necessary.

16.2 The organisers may postpone, suspend, or cancel the Game Jam due to circumstances beyond their reasonable control.

16.3 Participants will be informed of material changes through the contact details or platforms used for the Game Jam.

17. Acceptance of Terms

17.1 By registering for the Game Jam, participants confirm that they have read, understood, and agreed to these terms and conditions.

17.2 Where an entry is submitted by a team, every team member is responsible for complying with these terms and conditions.

results.title: TF-NUS Heritage Champions Showcase - Fireside Chat 1
results.description:
24 months of ideas and collaboration.
10 inspiring projects brought to life.
One day to celebrate it all!

 

 

Join us at the TF-NUS Heritage Champions Showcase as our Heritage Champions present projects celebrating the many facets of Singapore’s unique shared heritage! Come discover their work, hear the stories behind their projects, and explore the different ways our shared heritage can be understood and celebrated through the exhibition and fireside chats. We look forward to seeing you at the showcase!

 

The four teams that will be speaking at Fireside Chat #1 are:
 

  1. Shore to Shore from Batch 1
  2. Wartime Tuckshop from Batch 2
  3. Mama Mia from Batch 1
  4. Ten Years a Tree (TCM) from Batch 2
